cards.text: The angel Gabriel just told Mary of Nazareth that she'll give birth to a son named Jesus, and that her relative Elizabeth has conceived a son in her old age (Luke 1:26-36). In those days, Mary gets ready and HURRIES to a town in the hill country of Judah. Hurrying into HILL COUNTRY, friend, and I get winded hopping my gold base from one oven to the next.

cards.question: Mary arrives in the hill country of Judah to greet Elizabeth. Whose home does she walk into?

cards.text: That's Zechariah, Elizabeth's husband and a priest (Luke 1:5). Mary greets Elizabeth, and the moment Elizabeth hears it, something happens.

cards.question: Mary's greeting reaches Elizabeth's ears. What happens inside Elizabeth?

answers.text: Her baby leaps in her womb

cards.question: Right then, Elizabeth is filled with the ___.

cards.text: Then Elizabeth exclaims in a LOUD voice. Her indoor voice? Gone, left the building, didn't even take off its apron.

cards.question: Elizabeth tells Mary she's blessed among women. True or false: in the same breath, Elizabeth calls Mary's baby blessed too.
Then Elizabeth asks why she's so honored to have this visitor. What does she call Mary?

answers.text: A prophet of the Most High

cards.question: Elizabeth explains what happened when Mary's greeting reached her ears. She says her baby's leap was a leap of ___.
Elizabeth finishes by calling Mary blessed one more time. What does she say Mary is blessed for?

answers.text: Believing the Lord's word to her will be fulfilled
Traveling all the way to the hill country
Coming from the royal house of David

cards.text: Elizabeth just blessed Mary up one side and down the other. Now it's Mary's turn to talk.

cards.question: Elizabeth has finished speaking, and now Mary speaks. True or false: Mary starts by asking Elizabeth how she knew about the baby.

cards.text: Mary says, "My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior!" Her soul, her spirit, the WHOLE Mary is in on this.

cards.question: Mary gives the reason she's rejoicing. What does she say God has looked on with favor?

answers.text: The humble state of His servant
The strong faith of her family
The good deeds she has done

cards.question: True or false: Mary says only the people of her own town will ever call her blessed.

cards.text: Not one town. ALL generations will call her blessed. Meanwhile, the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with couldn't remember my name from Tuesday to Wednesday.

cards.question: Mary says great things have been done for her. Who does she say did them?

cards.text: And she adds, "Holy is His name." Then Mary moves from what God did for her to how He treats those who fear Him.

cards.question: Mary says God's mercy reaches those who fear Him. How long does she say it lasts?

cards.text: Mary says God has done mighty deeds with His arm and scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts. Scattered like a jar of sprinkles that just hit my bakery floor.

cards.question: Mary says God has brought rulers down from their thrones and lifted up the ___.
Mary says God has filled the hungry with good things. True or false: she says He fills the rich with good things too.

cards.text: Nope, the rich get sent away empty. Then Mary says God has helped His servant Israel, remembering to be merciful.

cards.question: Mary says this mercy is just what God promised long ago to ___ and his ___.
After all of that, Mary stays with Elizabeth for about three ___.

cards.text: Then Mary heads back home. We'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now, friend, but this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: The question says Mary arrives in the hill country 'to greet Elizabeth,' which gives a reason for her trip. Luke 1:39-40 says only that she hurried there, entered Zechariah's home and greeted Elizabeth. It never says why she went.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The blank is filled by a 2-word answer ('Holy Spirit'), but the wrong answers are 4 words ('fear of the Lord') and 3 words ('spirit of Elijah'). A blank holds 1 or 2 words, and the answers aren't about the same length.

rule.text: Fill in the blank: the question has a blank for 1 or 2 words. One blank has 3 answers. Two blanks have 5 single words to choose from.

findings.problem: The joke mixes two images. 'Left the building' (an idiom) is blended with a voice that 'didn't even take off its apron,' so a reader has to work out what a voice wearing an apron means.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The true-or-false asks about something Mary never says (asking Elizabeth how she knew about the baby). It doesn't move the passage forward or test a detail the baker needs, and it repeats the setup from card 1. The real content of Luke 1:46 is told on card 3 instead.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The humble state of His servant,' echoes the BSB wording and sounds more like the Bible than the plainer, modern wrong answers ('The strong faith of her family', 'The good deeds she has done'). That makes it stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to the drawer backstory: the batteries couldn't remember his name from Tuesday to Wednesday. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery, not new facts about the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The joke laughs at his old drawer friends (the batteries forgetting his name) instead of at himself. These are friends he was 'all in it together' with and still misses.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.
